A_open.text: First Saturday of October. Homecoming. Orange-and-black bunting everywhere.
Someone has tied a ribbon on every crow.
I've been handed a flag. No instructions. Just 'wave with feeling'.
The McVine tractor idles at the front, towing a float. A giant papier-mache Doris.
The banner reads: PUMPKINS. WE'RE VERY COMMITTED.
I look like a man dressed by his daughter.
Nearby, the Ravenwood Raven mascot paces, whispering. 'Don't lose the head. Don't lose the head.'
Walk along the parade line and greet the alumni. Press Action to talk.

stop_chet.text: Daniel Bart's boy! Spitting image! Your father was the greatest quarterback Ravenwood ever had!
He never told me he played football.
Threw a ball clear over the chapel! Hit a crow! That crow never forgave him.

stop_marge.text: You're Daniel's son! Quarterback? Nonsense. Your father was the raven mascot.
He never once took off the head. We didn't see his face until graduation.

stop_hal.text: Bart's boy. Those his boots? He wore those to the lab every day. Smelled like pumpkin.
Lab? The others said football. And a mascot.
Your father never attended a single game.
He was in the science building. Doing... whatever they did.
Ask him. He'll tell you what he told us. Which was nothing.

A2_dad.text: The three alumni stare at each other like people who each remember a different party.

A2_dad.prompt: Brad is holding the flag and a lot of questions.

do.text: Quarterback! That's amazing. I always knew he had an arm.
That's the spirit! Over the chapel!
Mascot.
Lab.
Okay. Which one of you is right?
All three freeze. They glance at one another, like people who once signed something.
Ask your father.
He'll tell you what he told us.
...Quarterback.

A2_dad.text: The Homecoming Parade is starting! Floats, line up!

else.text: Brad walks the route waving his flag with feeling. Nothing explodes. Mostly.

parade_j.text: Brad! Up here! Dad's gotta wave at the crowd. I'm the driver. You're my co-pilot.
Gord stands stiffly at the back of the float, waving like a statue.
Want to steer? Hands at ten and two. Just keep it straight.
I've never driven a tractor. Or a float. Or a Doris.
You'll be fine. Doris isn't a back seat driver.
Brad steers. The tractor wobbles. The float sways.
A paper pumpkin rolls off. The crowd cheers, assuming it's choreography.
Best Float goes to McVine Pumpkin Farm! For unmatched commitment to wobbling!
We never win! Dad's been entering for twenty years!

B_game.text: The football game is a long, slow event with a lot of people yelling at an orange ball.
Halftime! Time for the Pumpkin Toss! We need a volunteer from the crowd!
On the sideline, Gord, in hat and tie, points straight at Brad.
Legacy student Brad Bart, everyone! Son of a Ravenwood legend! Whichever legend that was!
Brad is handed a small pumpkin. The target is a bucket forty feet away.
I hauled forty pumpkins last week. I can toss one.
The pumpkin sails past the bucket. Past the goalpost.
It hits the raven mascot square in the head.
The mascot's head pops off and rolls across the field.
I'm so sorry! I'm so sorry! I quit!
The real crow lands on the fallen head and looks directly at Brad.
A Ravenwood record! Distance: forty-one feet. Accuracy: the mascot!

C_j.text: Dusk at the bonfire. The Best Float trophy, a small gold pumpkin, sits between Brad and Jane on a hay bale.
We never win anything. Dad is going to put it on the mantel and talk to it.
I think he already named it.
Gordon the Second. It's probably true.
Brad. Can I tell you something? I don't know if I want the farm.
Everyone assumes I'll take over. Dad, the town, the pumpkins. And lately the soil feels wrong.
I don't know whether I'm staying because I love it, or because I never asked myself.

C_j.prompt: Jane watches the fire, not Brad.

do.text: Whatever you choose, make it yours. Not your dad's, not the pumpkins'.
Nobody's said that to me. Not once.
You'll be great either way. The farm's lucky to have you. So is anyone else.
That's nice. Thank you.
Pumpkins assume a lot. It's their whole thing.
Ha! They're so full of themselves.
She laughs, but her eyes say she wanted a real answer.

C_j.text: Jane rests her head on Brad's shoulder. The bonfire roars. The gold pumpkin gleams.
Thanks for coming with me today.

C_s.text: The Log and Stump is almost empty. In the corner, Sandra sits alone with black coffee.
Homecoming is a pagan ritual of fire and mediocre football.
I'm observing from a safe distance.
You said you'd come with me.
I did. I'm here. You're here. This is the date.
It's a great date. The ambiance is very you.
Come here. I owe you a photo.
Behind the bar hangs a framed photo. Three young people stand before a faded banner.
The banner reads: PUMPKIN RESEARCH PROGRAM.
That's my dad. He looks just like me.
Beside him is a bearded young man, who has to be Gord. The third is a woman with glasses and a clipboard.
My grandfather wrote on the back. 'Dr. E. Peters.' That's all I know.

C_s.prompt: Sandra turns away from the photo. She knows more than she's saying.

do.text: You know something. What did your grandfather say?
Tavern rule. What's said at the bar stays at the bar.
Don't push me. I'll tell you when I'm ready.
Brad says nothing. He sits down across from her. The silence stretches. Then, softly:
My grandfather said it ended badly. And that nobody who was there will talk about it.
You didn't push. I like that. Come on. I'll show you the best seat in town.

C_s.text: From the tavern roof, the bonfire glows across the rooftops. Sandra sits beside Brad, hood down.
Best seat in town. No marching band. No mascot. Just fire from far away.
I like Homecoming better from here.

C_g.text: After the game, the Grove Cafe booth is mobbed. And the Raven mascot has quit.
Brad! You're tall! You're the same size! The costume is yours!
Georgia, I just knocked the last raven's head off.
Which is why you owe the raven. And me. Mostly me.
Brad pulls on the raven costume. The head smells of old cider. He can barely see.
I can't see anything. Is it supposed to be this dark?
Perfect! People love a raven! Just flap!
A small child hugs Brad's leg. 'The raven smells like cider.' 'That's me,' says Brad, in a muffled voice.
The real crow lands on the booth and salutes with one wing. Georgia is laughing too hard to speak.
We sold two hundred muffins. A record. Thanks, Raven Brad.
Can you stay with me a bit? My shift's over. I don't want to go home yet.

C_g.prompt: Brad is still wearing the raven head.

do.text: Okay. Hold on. Let me take this off.
Everyone calls me the cafe girl. And I love the cafe. But sometimes I think I'm only a pastry.
You're way more than a pastry. You noticed I was lost on the first day, and you made me feel at home.
...Thanks. I didn't know it showed.
Caw. This raven thinks you are an excellent baker.
Stop! You're ruining my serious moment!
It's okay. I needed a laugh more than a talk.

C_g.text: Georgia leans back on the grass, the raven head in her lap. The bonfire crackles.
I'm planning something big for next week. A dessert. Top secret. You'll be the first taster.

C_p.text: At the reception tent, Patricia waits with a lanyard, a clipboard, and great duty.
Mr. Bart. Punctual. Remember. This is a walk, not a date.
A walk to the bonfire, between colleagues.
Precisely. Hold this clipboard. You look responsible.
Patricia Peters! Dr. Peters's daughter! Your mother's program, did anyone ever explain what happened?
Mr. Hal. The punch is that way.
Hal retreats. Patricia exhales. For a moment she looks tired.
My mother's work was decades ago. People remember it badly. Or too well.
Mr. Bart. Be careful which stories you chase.

C_p.prompt: Patricia returns to her clipboard, but she is clearly listening.

do.text: What do you mean? Which stories?
The kind that go wrong. I can't say more. Not yet.
You're on duty. I'll walk you to the bonfire. Nothing else.
You noticed. Most people push. Thank you, Mr. Bart.

C_p.text: They stand at the edge of the firelight. Patricia's glasses catch the flames.
It is, in its way, a lovely evening.

D_close.text: Night. The bonfire towers over the quad. Students cheer, sing, and burn marshmallows.

then.text: Here. I took a picture of the tavern photo for you. Don't say I never gave you anything.
On her phone: three young people before a banner. One has Brad's face.
That's my dad. And that's Gord.
The back says 'Dr. E. Peters'. I'm saying nothing.

D_close.text: Brad reaches into his jacket pocket for his phone. His fingers find a folded paper.
In block capitals: THE SOIL REMEMBERS. ASK YOUR FATHER ABOUT THE DANCE.
Beneath it is a tiny doodle of a pumpkin.
Who put this in my pocket? Everyone's been within arm's reach today.

then.text: The alumni all told me different stories. And now a dance. They're all hiding something.

else.text: Dad's stories were always about football. Never a dance.

D_close.text: Brad: Dad, what dance? Someone left me a note.
Dad: What dance? Gotta run! Love you! Eat your vegetables! (Not pumpkin.)
He's definitely hiding something. Everyone is.
Across the fire, Gord is watching Brad. Caught, he turns very fast to inspect a pumpkin.
On a fence rail, the crow sits holding a name tag. It looks very innocent.
